newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU takes France to court over nursing test.
newsitem.headline: EU takes France to court over nursing test.

text.p: The European Commission decided on Thursday to take France to the European Court of Justice for failing to comply with European Union law concerning freedom of establishment and of movement of workers in the 15-nation bloc.

Paris had failed to change rules requiring nurses qualified in a specialism not regulated in France to pass an examiniation on all aspects of nurses' training to obtain authorisation to practise as nurses responsible for general care, it said.

The problem arises in the case of specialist nurses who do not hold one of the general care nursing qualifications listed in the relevant EU directive and because of this do not qualify for automatic recognition in France.

"The French legislation does not take proper account of the training undergone in the migrant's home state," it said, adding this was in breach of rules laid down by the EU treaty regarding freedom of movement for workers and freedom of establishment.

Separately, the Commission said it had decided to send a so-called reasoned opinion to Italy for failing to incorporate correctly into national law EU rules concerning the mutual recognition of diplomas and certicates for architects.
This is the second stage in EU infringement proceedings, before referring the case to the Luxembourg-based court.
It said Italian legislation unduly restricted the freedom to provide services by prohibiting persons exercising that freedom from having a permanent base in Italy.
"Were Italy not to respond satisfactorily within two months of receiving that opinion, the Commission should then refer the matter to the Court of Justice," it said.
